title: customer-omega-incident-timeline-scratchpad-evelyn-park
body:
Context:
- Customer: Customer Omega (internal account id: cust-omega-9).
- Symptom: production calls to /v1/generate returning 503/504 and occasional CUDA OOMs on dedicated pool (dedicated-omega-pool).
- Impact: intermittent failures ~ 11:00–13:30 PST on 2025-11-03, elevated latencies (p50 1200ms -> 3600ms).

Objective: compile a concise timeline + breadcrumbs for an internal update and draft a customer-facing status note. Include commands tried, exact error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

---
Raw timeline / breadcrumbs (local timestamps PST):
2025-11-03 10:58 AM - First alerts: Grafana SLO alerts (p95 latency > 2s) for route /v1/generate (model: redwood-turbo-13b).
2025-11-03 11:05 AM - Customer #omega on support channel reports "lots of failed requests" and quotes 503 errors.
2025-11-03 11:10 AM - SRE on-call (Ravi) started initial investigation.
2025-11-03 11:15 AM - Observed error surge. Deployed additional logs (increase log level for runtime) and started tailing.
2025-11-03 11:22 AM - Attempted scale-up of dedicated-omega-pool: increased desired replicas from 6 -> 8 (k8s autoscaler).
2025-11-03 11:28 AM - Noted repeated CUDA OOMs on one node, pod restarted.
2025-11-03 11:35 AM - Rolled back a recent model config change (model-concurrency bump) as mitigation.
2025-11-03 11:42 AM - Errors decreased briefly then resurged at 12:05 PM.
2025-11-03 12:12 PM - Enabled fallback routing to hosted pool for low-priority traffic (not customer-omega production traffic).
2025-11-03 12:30 PM - Investigated request traces: big spikes correlated with long-context (> 8k tokens) requests.
2025-11-03 12:45 PM - Customer provided an example payload that uses system prompt + large user history (~9k tokens).
2025-11-03 12:50 PM - Applied temporary throttling rule for extremely long seq requests for that route.
2025-11-03 01:12 PM - After throttling and rolling back config, p95 returned closer to normal, but a small fraction of requests still 503.

---
Commands run (most relevant):
- kubectl (context: prod-dedicated-omega):
  kubectl -n redwood-inference get pods -l pool=dedicated-omega-pool -o wide
  # output: multiple pods, one in CrashLoopBackOff

- To inspect logs on offending pod:
  kubectl -n redwood-inference logs pod/serve-omega-5 -c inference-runtime --since=30m | tail -n 200\  
  # snippets below (truncated)

- docker/container-level inspect (on node):
  sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 | grep -i oom || true

- traced one request (trace id: trace-0a7b):
  curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d @sample.json

---
Key error snippets (copied/pasted):
1) From pod logs (serve-omega-5):
[2025-11-03T11:27:49Z] ERROR inference.runtime: worker 3 failed to allocate memory for KV cache: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 23.68 GiB total capacity; 20.10 GiB already allocated; 1024 MiB free)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/runtime/inference.py", line 858, in forward
    kv_cache.grow(new_kv_size)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory

2) From kubernetes events for node ip-10-2-7-14:
Warning  OOMKills  3m   kubelet  Container oomkilled "inference-runtime"

3) Nginx gateway (ingress logs):
"GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 503 0 "-" "python-requests/2.29.0" rt=1.223 ua="-"

4) Trace-level (example request with long context):
request_id=trace-0a7b latency_ms=4220 input_tokens=9124 generation_tokens=320 model=redwood-turbo-13b pool=dedicated-omega-pool error="OOM during KV cache alloc"

---
Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: Customer is sending unusually long-context requests (>=8k tokens) causing KV cache growth and CUDA OOMs on dedicated pool nodes. Some pods hit OOM and restart -> transient 503s.
2) Secondary: Recent model concurrency/config change increased per-worker memory reservation (we bumped model-concurrency from 2->4), so memory headroom reduced. Interplay with long contexts amplified failures.
3) Tertiary: Node-level memory fragmentation or older CUDA driver mismatch causing perceived "already allocated" memory (less likely — would expect more widespread failures).
4) Unlikely: Malicious traffic or burst beyond expected QPS — metrics didn't show large QPS spike, just longer per-request memory.

Investigation evidence supporting primary hypothesis:
- Customer-provided payload has ~9k tokens.
- Traces show high input_tokens and latencies.
- Pod logs show direct OOM when allocating KV cache.
- Failures concentrated on dedicated pool (where memory is tuned for baseline contexts).

Mitigations applied so far (and effect):
- Rolled back concurrency bump (11:35 AM) -> small improvement.
- Scaled replicas 6->8 (11:22 AM) -> helped absorb some load but OOMs persisted on a subset of requests.
- Temporary throttling of >8k token requests for route (12:50 PM) -> p95 improved, errors reduced.
- Increased log level and traced representative requests -> confirmed large contexts.

Proposed next steps (short-term):
- Keep throttling >8k token requests for 24h as a protective measure (ops rule).
- Temporarily enforce per-request token cap at the gateway for customer-omega route (customer-visible but avoidable).
- Add automatic fallback for long-context requests to a pool with larger memory (if available) or to hosted pool with larger instance types.
- Re-run canary of model-concurrency=2 for 24h to validate stability.
- Post-incident: evaluate model quantization profile and KV cache memory growth behavior for redwood-turbo-13b on dedicated-omega-pool hardware.

Proposed customer-facing draft (short):
Subject: Update: Incident impacting some /v1/generate requests (Customer Omega)
Hi <Customer Omega contact>,
We observed intermittent failures for some generate requests earlier today between ~11:00–13:30 PST. Root cause appears to be large request contexts (multi-thousand token histories) which, combined with a recent config change that increased concurrency, led to memory pressure on the dedicated GPU pool and resulted in a subset of requests failing with 503/timeout.
What we did: rolled back a recent concurrency config, scaled the pool, and implemented a temporary protection to reject extremely large requests while we work on a long-term fix.
Current status: the majority of traffic is stable; we are continuing monitoring and will keep this protection in place until stability is confirmed.
Next steps: we will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix (either increased memory headroom for the pool, a larger-instance fallback, or model-level optimizations).
Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience — cc'ing your support contact.

Internal notes for postmortem:
- Capture exact request size distribution for customer-omega last 7 days (histogram).
- Reproduce locally with 9k token payload and run memory profiling (kv cache growth).
- Check recent deploys/PRs that touched model-concurrency and autoscaling policy.
- Validate node-level driver/ffmpeg/cuda versions on affected hosts; confirm no other tenants impacted.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who authorized the model-concurrency bump? (Trace PR + owner) -> assigned to Maya to pull PR in 30m.
- Can we provision a temporary larger-instance fallback for the pool within 2–4 hours? (Infra) -> Ravi to escalate.
- Should we add an automatic request-size-based routing rule (route >X tokens to fallback)? Product/Platform decision.

Draft internal slack update (short):
SRE update: we've traced the 11:00–13:30 PST Customer Omega failures to long-context requests (~9k tokens) causing CUDA OOMs on dedicated-omega-pool. Rolled back concurrency change and added token-throttling. p95 improved; continuing to monitor.

Notes for follow-up investigation commands:
- get 7d request size histogram from clickhouse:
  SELECT bucket, count(*) FROM request_tokens WHERE customer_id='cust-omega-9' GROUP BY bucket;
- reproduce memory profile in canary: run local workload with sample.json (9k tokens) under model-concurrency=2 config and capture /proc/mem and nvidia-smi top during run.

---
End of scratchpad.
(Will refine into a short internal incident post and customer advisory once we confirm repro + mitigation timeline.)
